Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
130 PM EDT Fri Jul 31 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 231 AM EDT Friday...

Rainfall this weekend has been slowed down by about 12 to 18 hours 
as a more amplified upper level trough will delay the better forcing 
and moisture. Sunday is now looking mostly dry for much of the North 
Country and northern New York.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 231 AM EDT Friday...

1. Seasonal weather expected today and Saturday.

2. Widespread rainfall expected late Sunday and Monday.

3. Increasing heat and humidity for the August 4th thru 6th 
period.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 231 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A foggy start is expected across the region this morning 
as saturated soils, light winds, and clear skies help promote for 
formation. With sunrise shortly after 5:30 AM, it's likely most fog 
will dissipate prior to the morning commute. Still, some patchy 
dense fog in sheltered valleys and river valleys could continue 
through 9 AM. Afterwards, we've got some beautiful weather on tap as 
surface high pressure noses in from the west. Mostly clear skies 
with highs in the upper 70s to mid 80s are expected both today and 
Saturday with an isolated shower or two across the higher peaks of 
the Adirondacks. Limited mid-level steering flow will keep the 
showers anchored across the higher terrain and will be short-lived 
as increasing subsidence will kill any convection that tries to 
develop. Northwest winds less than 10 mph will be seen today with 
winds backing to the south at 5 to 15 mph on Saturday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Quite a bit has changed in the last 24 hours as 
deterministic guidance is struggling to understand the evolution of 
a deepening upper level trough/low and short-wave energy. The latest 
trends show a strengthening upper level trough that ultimately closes 
off as shortwave energy rounds the base of the upper level trough 
and increases vorticity. This ultimately leads to a higher amplitude 
longwave trough which slows down the progression of both the deep 
moisture and better frontal dynamics. The general thinking is that 
most of Sunday is dry; albeit a bit humid as dewpoints start 
approaching 70 degrees. Rainfall is now expected to move in Sunday 
night from west to east and continue well into Monday as a surface 
low develops across western New York and quickly move north towards 
Montreal. A plume of 1.7" to 1.9" PWATs is still expected to advect 
northward across New England during this timeframe which should 
support efficient rain processes. The general thinking of 0.5 to 1.5 
inches of rainfall still seems likely and the flood threat seems 
more contingent on rainfall rates vs actual rainfall amounts. 
Looking at the GFS and ECMWF ensembles, there are still about 10-20 
percent of members showing over 2 inches of rainfall so there are 
still some concerns to watch out for as we head into early next 
week. The picture should become more clear tomorrow as we get better 
upper air sampling which should help the models begin locking in on 
a solution vs being so volatile from run-to-run.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A building low-mid level ridge in the wake of the 
northern stream shortwave trough departing the area to the east will 
yield warming temperatures Tuesday (8/4) through Thursday (8/6) next 
week. GEFS 850mb mean temperatures support valley high temperatures 
in the lower 80s for Tuesday, and then in the upper 80s for 
Wednesday and Thursday. With increasing humidity through the period, 
the best chance of thunderstorms will likely be Thursday, with PoPs 
40-50% for Thursday afternoon. Otherwise, no significant weather is 
currently anticipated during the Days 4-7 forecast period.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 18Z Saturday...Aside from a few showers in eastern
Vermont and near the Adirondacks, conditions will remain quiet
today. A stray shower may occur at EFK/MPV/SLK through 20Z with
best chances of occurrence at EFK where showers are ongoing. By
20Z the wave responsible will be shift southeastward drier air,
evident on water vapor imagery, working into the region.
Otherwise, the main forecast concern will be for overnight fog.
MPV and EFK are most likely to see IFR or lower CIG/VIS
restrictions given clearing skies and a solid radiational
cooling set up 02-14Z. SLK still appears likely to be affected 
by fog, but could have a lingering low/mid CIG that may delay 
onset of fog. 

Outlook...

Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Definite
